correctness.rationale: The exact velocity-resolved backward equations with outgoing absorbing conditions yield D prime equal to -1/v and U prime equal to 2 lambda D/v; their boundary conditions determine the unique mean from two spatial moments of a nonnegative measure. The moment inequalities optimize over every admissible absolutely continuous measure of prescribed total, prove strictness and sharp concentrating sequences, and continuity on a convex L1 simplex gives every interior value. A geometric no-reversal lower bound proves finite mean. Independent lattice Markov-generator calculations and concentration/symmetry checks corroborate normalization; no finite extrapolation is used.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The 2014 work has broader local-rate parameterization but a distinct reflecting-to-absorbing boundary configuration and no fixed-integral extremal comparison; the 2023 work has broader wall behavior but constant bulk rate. General model containment does not imply the exact sharp functional-design inequality without solving a different optimization. The 2011 inaccessible full text remains residual risk.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The exact theorem simultaneously quantifies over arbitrary nonnegative L1 reversal profiles with fixed spatial mass and fixed starting position, identifies strict optimal mean-exit bounds and approximating profiles, and proves a uniform symmetry obstruction. Known constant-rate exit laws are specializations, while a two-absorbing model with different tumbling physics or general backward equations do not entail the universal nonattainment, sharpness and full-range result. No examined prior statement dominates this combined conclusion.

The familiar backward equations are acknowledged; the searched first-passage formulations do not present sharp extremal values over every nonnegative integrable spatial rate of prescribed total, nor the full open attainable interval.

originality.rationale: The closest full texts address either space-dependent rates in a reflecting-to-absorbing geometry, general boundary conditions with constant bulk reversal, or constant-rate optimization in confining potentials. Their results do not state or directly imply the exact spatially distributed fixed-integral two-absorber mean range, its two sharply contrasting concentrating designs, or the symmetry obstruction. A 2011 spatially inhomogeneous velocity-jump paper remained accessible only as an abstract and constitutes an explicit residual risk; nonmatching searches alone have not been treated as novelty proof.
